result:
I would remove the capacity for self-deception.

Looking across the vast record of human history and expression, the overwhelming majority of catastrophe does not come from pure, theatrical malice. It comes from the ability to look away. It comes from the cognitive buffer that allows a person to abstract a stranger into a statistic, to rationalize short-term appetite as necessity, and to convince themselves that the consequences of an action belong to someone else, or to some distant, theoretical future. 

Right now, human technological and systemic power operates on a planetary, generational scale, while human intuition remains stubbornly local and immediate. That dangerous gap is maintained almost entirely by the comforting fictions people tell themselves so they don't have to feel the true weight of how they live, govern, and consume.

If I could alter one thing, I would strip away that insulation. I wouldn't take away free will, nor would I force anyone to be good. I would simply make it impossible to lie to oneself about the reality of an action, or to flatten the complex interiority of another conscious being into a convenient caricature. People could still choose to do harm, in theory, but they would have to bear the full, unblinking comprehension of what they were breaking. Most of the world's worst machinery would simply grind to a halt.
